look_here_first: LOOK FIRST underground: trace a full stolon from shoot to tuber. Softer/spongier stolons and commonly 6–11 mm tubers support yellow nutsedge; compare several mature persistent floral scales (~1.8–2.7 mm), often yellowish brown. Do not ID by yellow head alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO/FNA report Texas native at state level. No BONAP/NAPA three target-county proof certified.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial sedge with basal linear leaves and flowering culms, often in disturbed moist lawns or sites.
morphology_keys.underground: Stoloniferous with softer/spongier stolons, tubers usually 6–11 mm; photograph intact stolon chain.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Umbel-like crown of leaflike bracts, rays and flattened spikelets; often yellow or straw colored but color overlaps.
morphology_keys.scales: Persistent mature floral scales generally 1.8–2.7 mm; use 1 mm ruler; native variety not assigned.
morphology_keys.fruit: Single achene per fertile scale; scaled mature fruit comparison useful.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Purple nutsedge generally has hard/wiry underground stolons, tubers commonly 3–8 mm, and often red-purple scales 2.6–3.4 mm. Overlap requires the combined underground and reproductive key.
comparisons.cautions: Photo source geography is not evidence of three-county target zone native range; colors and many measurements overlap, require mature specimens.
